ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a block with a mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ starts from the bottom of an inclined plane with an initial velocity $v_{0}$ and moves up a sufficiently long inclined plane. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is 0.25. It is known that $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$, and $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. If the initial velocity of the block is $v_{0}=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, and air resistance is neglected.

1. The magnitude of the acceleration $a$ of the block moving up along the inclined plane
2. The time $t$ it takes for the block to travel from the starting point to the bottom of the inclined plane and back

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an inclined plane; the small block is located near the bottom end of the inclined plane, and the velocity arrow v0 points upward along the inclined plane; on the right side, v-t coordinate axes are drawn. The inclined plane is sufficiently long; the object first slides upward along the inclined plane, and after stopping, then slides downward along the inclined plane back to the bottom end. Reasoning: Take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. When the object slides upward, the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin37°, and the sliding friction force is also downward along the inclined plane, with magnitude μmg cos37°. Therefore, in the upward-sliding stage, the acceleration direction is downward along the inclined plane, and its magnitude is a = g sin37° + μg cos37° = 10×0.6 + 0.25×10×0.8 = 6 + 2 = 8 m/s². When sliding upward to the highest point, the velocity becomes 0: 0 = 8 - 8t_up, so t_up = 1 s. The upward-sliding distance is obtained from 0 = 8² - 2×8×s, giving s = 4 m. When sliding downward and returning, gravity is downward along the inclined plane, and friction is upward along the inclined plane, so the acceleration downward along the inclined plane is a_down = g sin37° - μg cos37° = 10×0.6 - 0.25×10×0.8 = 6 - 2 = 4 m/s². Sliding downward from rest through the same distance 4 m: 4 = (1/2)×4×t_down², giving t_down = √2 s. The total time t = t_up + t_down = 1 + √2 s.
